title: Mexico’s State Workers’ Social Security Institute Launches 100 Clinics for the Universal Health Service
author: Carolina Gómez Mena
content:
_This article by[Carolina Gómez
Mena](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Carolina%20G%C3%B3mez%20Mena)
originally appeared in the [October 6, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/06/politica/issste-pone-
en-marcha-100-consultorios-para-el-servicio-universal-de-salud), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

The director general of the Institute for Social Security and Services for
State Workers (ISSSTE), Martí Batres Guadarrama, highlighted the launch of
**100 clinics** of the agency that will be integrated into the Universal
Health Service (SUS), an initiative promoted by President Claudia Sheinbaum
Pardo with the purpose of bringing medical care closer to the population.

> As reported today at the morning press conference of President
> @Claudiashein, the Universal Health Service is advancing with the
> construction of clinics to expand the primary health network. The @ISSSTE_mx
> will contribute 500 clinics. We have finished 100 and by the end of the
> year, we will have another 100.
>
> Martí Batres, on social media

The federal government will establish **12,750 medical clinics of the new SUS
in 24 states** , which will begin operating in January 2027. The ISSSTE's
contribution represents 3.9 percent of the total of those medical spaces.

Batres detailed that the new clinics are distributed as follows: 33 in
Michoacán, 20 in Oaxaca, 10 in Puebla, 10 in Tlaxcala, 10 in Yucatán, six in
Mexico City, five in Quintana Roo, three in Guerrero and three in Chiapas.

In addition, he stressed that these are already providing medical service to
people, **regardless of whether or not they are beneficiaries**.

## They Will Treat Common Ailments and Chronic Diseases

He indicated that the ISSSTE clinics are part of the 12,750 that will be
installed in the country to treat the population for common ailments and to
follow up on chronic diseases, such as diabetes and hypertension.

“These are 12,750 clinics distributed throughout the national territory so
that people can go to be treated for so-called acute ailments: headaches,
stomachaches, a cold, pains of that kind, ailments of that kind that have to
be treated immediately and that cannot wait for a regular appointment to be
scheduled at a clinic,” he said.

He noted that the ISSSTE, the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) and
IMSS-Bienestar will promote these clinics, which will provide care to anyone,
regardless of their affiliation, starting in January 2027.
